transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As we all know, we're meeting today to discuss the six-week pilot aimed at reducing classroom disruptions from student cell-phone use. The draft proposal on the table covers grades 9 and 10, suggests placing phones in open classroom bins, and lists September 2, 2026 as the tentative launch date. Before I can approve the final scope, procedures, and launch record, I'd like to hear from each of you — our participating teacher, our counselor, and our technology coordinator — with your reports. Let's work through this systematically so we can make informed decisions today.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I want to share something important from my own classroom experience. I ran a trial with all of my 9th-grade sections and recorded 23 phone-related interruptions in just two weeks. I also found that numbered locking pouches significantly reduced those interruptions. Based on that, I recommended a grade-9-only pilot using one pouch per student in my team notes — but those notes haven't been added to the draft proposal yet.

transcript.text: I need to raise an important safety concern before we finalize procedures. Two students have active safety plans requiring them to receive time-sensitive messages from their caregivers during the school day. I confirmed these plans with both families this week, but this exception has not yet been entered into the pilot procedure. We need to make sure any phone collection policy accounts for these students before approval.

The student-information system's phone-registration module will not be ready until September 16, 2026, and our technology change plan requires the pilot to launch with a digital registration record on that date. I confirmed the deployment date with the district systems team just this week. The draft proposal still shows September 2, but we cannot launch without the registration module in place.
